sentences.text: After the trial, the accused were acquitted of all the alleged offences.

Seeking setting aside of the impugned judgment dated 25.02.2017, the State has preferred the present appeal under Sections 378(1) & (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'Cr.P.C.).
2.
The summary of the case of the prosecution in the Trial Court was that the deceased Smt. Jayashri was given in marriage to accused No.1-Chidananda on 12.12.2014.

During the marriage talks, it was agreed a sum of `51,000/-, one tola of gold to be given to the bridegroom which was in addition to `11,000/- payable to the bridegroom towards the clothes; a necklace for the bride was also agreed to be given.
A sum of `11,000/- was given through bank credit to the accused No.1 towards clothing and another sum of `5,000/- was also paid as the amount towards treasury.
Despite the same, the accused Nos.1 to 4, who were the husband, mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and husband of accused No.3 respectively, were subjecting the deceased Smt. Jayashri to cruelty.

On the night of the date 17.04.2015, the deceased Smt. Jayashri met an unnatural death by sustaining stab injury on her abdomen and thus, the accused Nos.1 to 4 have committed the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act and under Sections 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of IPC, and that accused No.1 has committed the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC.
3.

Since the accused pleaded not guilty, the trial was held wherein, in order to prove the alleged guilt against the accused, the prosecution got examined twentyone witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.21 and got marked twentyseven documents from Exs.P.1 to P.27 and material objects M.Os.1 to 10.
Statement of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded.

On behalf of the accused, three witnesses were examined as D.W.1 to D.W.3 and six documents were got marked as Exs.D.1 to D.6.
4.
After hearing both side, the learned Sessions Judge's Court, by its impugned judgment dated 25.02.2017, acquitted the accused for the offences charged against them.
5. The respondents/accused are being represented by their counsel.
6. The Sessions Judge's Court records were called for and the same are placed before this Court.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the material placed before this Court and also the Sessions Judge's Court records.

8. The points that arise for our consideration are:
i) Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 to 4 have demanded dowry in a sum of `51,000/-, one tola of gold, a sum of `11,000/- towards clothes to the bridegroom and a gold necklace to the bride and taken the dowry of a sum of `51,000/- & `11,000/- by accused No.1 and a sum of `5,000/- in the form of credit to the bank account of accused No.2 and thereby have committed the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act?

the wife of accused No.1, to cruelty after her marriage with accused No.1 on 12.12.2014 and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC?

iii) Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 to 4, in furtherance of their common intention and in connection with demand for dowry, inflicted injury upon Smt. Jayashri on the date 17.04.2015 at about 11.15 p.m.,
in their house at Vidyanagara, Kotturu Town, Kudligi Taluk, within the limits of complaint Police Station and the injured Smt. Jayashri succumbed to the same on the same night i.e. at about 3.15 a.m. on 18.04.2015 and thus, have committed the offence punishable under Section 304B read with Section 34 of IPC?

iv) Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused No.1- Chidananda,
on the date 17.04.2015, at about 11.15 p.m., while his wife deceased Smt. Jayashri was sleeping in his house at Vidyanagara, Kotturu Town, Kudligi Taluk, within the limits of complaint Police Station,
intentionally stabbed said Smt. Jayashri with a knife to cause her murder and due to the injuries inflicted upon her said Smt. Jayashri succumbed to the same at about 3.15 a.m. on 18.04.2015 and thus, has committed the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC?
v) Whether the judgment of acquittal challenged under the appeal, passed by the learned III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ballari, sitting at Hosapete, in S.C. No.5048/2015 on 25.02.2017 warrants any interference at the hands of this Court?

9. The present appeal is filed by the State challenging the judgment of acquittal of the accused from the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act.

Since as per criminal law, the accused are presumed to be innocent until their guilt is proved and further the accused, in the instant case, have already been benefited by the impugned judgment of acquittal in their favour, this Court, as a Court of appeal upon the impugned judgment of acquittal, must be very careful and cautious in analysing and appreciating the evidence led in the matter.

The Hon'ble Apex Court, in its judgment in CHANDRAPPA AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA, reported in (2007) 4 SCC 415, while laying down the general principles regarding powers of the Appellate Court while dealing in an appeal against an order of an acquittal, was pleased to observe at paragraph 42.(4) and paragraph 42.(5) as below:
"(4) An appellate court, however, must bear in mind that in case of acquittal, there is double presumption in favour of the accused.

sentences.text: Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law.
Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial court.

Jayashri is the wife of accused No.1-Chidananda having married to him on the date 12.12.2014 and that accused No.2-Smt.Shantamma Hiremath, accused No.3- Smt.Vijayalakshmi @ Latha @ Baby are the mother and sister respectively of accused No.1 and accused No.4 is the husband of accused No.3 which has come out in the evidence of P.W.1 (C.W.1), P.W.3 (C.W.5) and P.W.4 (C.W.10) have remained undenied and undisputed.
Rather they are the admitted facts also.
However, the accused have vehemently denied and disputed that all of them or any one of them have committed the alleged offences charged against them.

13. Among the twentyone witnesses examined by the prosecution, the witnesses who speak about the alleged demand and acceptance of dowry are P.W.1 (C.W.1) - Sri. Nagaraj, P.W.3 (C.W.5)-Smt.Madevamma and P.W.4 (C.W.10)-Sri. Rudrayya.

All these witnesses in their evidence,
have stated that at the time of marriage, talks were held about giving a sum of `51,000/-, one tola of gold, a sum of `11,000/- towards clothing and bearing marriage expenses.

P.W.1, who undisputedly is the younger brother of the deceased Smt. Jayashri, though has not stated in his examination-in-chief as to whether the alleged valuables were given, however, in his cross-examination, has stated that the dowry amount was paid on the day of marriage and the amount towards clothing was given on the twentyfourth day in the hands of the elders.

However,
suggestions denying his statements of alleged marriage talks and the alleged payment of the alleged dowry were made to the witness, but he did not admit those suggestions as true.

P.W.3, the mother of the deceased, has stated in her evidence that at the time of marriage `50,000/-
and one tola of gold was given.
P.W.4, the uncle of P.W.1 and the deceased, has stated that at the time of marriage a sum of `51,000/- and one tola of gold was given.
Thereafter, P.W.1 had given an additional sum of `10,000/- and another sum of `5,000/- to accused No.1.
All these three witnesses have stated that after the marriage, accused were harassing the deceased Smt.Jayashri.

However, P.W.1 and P.W.3, the brother and mother of the deceased respectively, have State Of Karnataka vs Chidananda V. Hiremath on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128378016/

sentences.text: However, even according to him, it is a hearsay information to him.
Nowhere, the witness has given any details as to how he came to know about the alleged harassing for valuables by the accused upon the deceased.
14. The prosecution in support of its contention, has got produced a marriage agreement showing the list of the valuables to be given to the bridegroom and the bride parties.

A reading of the said document at Ex.P.5 would go to show that it is only recorded as to what are the valuables to be given to both the parties to the marriage; it does not mention as to who should give the articles mentioned therein, whether it is from the bride side or bridegroom side.
Moreover, nowhere the said document mentions as to at whose demand or request those valuables are agreed to be given to the parties to the marriage.
It does not whisper about any demand made from the accused side for those valuables.

15. In addition to the above, even though P.W.1, P.W.3 and P.W.4 have stated as to what valuables were to be given at the time of marriage, but none of these witnesses have, in specific terms, stated that any demand was made from the accused for those valuables or that those valuables were agreed to be given as dowry to the accused.
All these three witnesses have stated that as per the talks, those valuables have to be given.

Furthermore, the complainant in his complaint at Ex.P.1, has stated that the marriage of the deceased with accused No.1 was performed after giving the 'varopachara' (gifts as pleasantries) as per the custom prevailing in their caste.
Nowhere in his complaint, the complainant had whispered that the alleged valuables were given as dowry or that there was any demand from the accused for any dowry.

As observed above, the complainant as P.W.1, nowhere in his examination-in-chief, had whispered the word 'dowry' or has mentioned that there was demand made from the accused either prior to or at the time of marriage, or after the marriage of the deceased with accused No.1 for any dowry.

Though the said witness, in his cross-examination, at one place has stated that the dowry amount was given, however, in the absence of essential details as to who asked for dowry and when such demand was made and in what form the alleged demand was made, the mere stray words used by P.W.1, in his cross-examination, as "dowry amount was given"
would not lead the Court to infer that such a demand for dowry was made from the accused or any such amount for dowry was given to the accused from the complainant side.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the alleged valuables were given by the complainant side to the accused, and that any demand was there from the accused side for those valuables and, more particularly, in the light of the complainant himself in his complaint stating that articles/pleasantries given were as per the custom prevailing in their caste, it cannot be held that there was any demand or payment of dowry from the complainant side to the accused in connection with the marriage of the deceased with accused No.1.

As such, we do not find any reason to interfere in the said finding of Sessions Judge's Court in holding that the prosecution has failed to prove the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of the DP Act by the accused.

sentences.text:
Section 498A of IPC reads as follows:
"498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.

-
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

- For the purpose of this section "cruelty" means- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to case grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

Thus, in order to prove the alleged cruelty punishable under Section 498A of IPC against the accused, the prosecution is required to establish that the conduct of the accused towards the deceased was willful and that it was of such a nature as was likely to drive the deceased to commit suicide or grave injury or danger to her life, limb or health OR the prosecution is required to prove that the harassment to the deceased was with a view to coercing her to meet any unlawful demand or property or valuable security or on account of failure by her to meet such demand.
18.

The learned Additional State Public Prosecutor, in his argument, submitted that undisputedly,
the death of the deceased was unnatural which, according to the prosecution, is homicidal as such,
the harassment meted to her by the accused has resulted in she meeting a homicidal death.

Thus,
the cruelty practiced by the accused has been established beyond reasonable doubt.

19. Per contra, the learned counsel for the accused, in his arguments, submitted that none of the witnesses examined by the prosecution have whispered any details of cruelty; except stating that the deceased was put to some inconvenience, no other details with respect to either the alleged willful conduct or harassment has been narrated by the witnesses as such, there is no evidence to hold that the deceased was subjected to cruelty by the accused.

P.W.1, in his evidence, has stated that his sister i.e., the deceased Smt. sentences.text: It is due to their irritation, a sum of `5,000/- was credited to the account of accused No.2 towards treasury.
Except this statement about the alleged conduct of the accused or harassment by them towards the deceased, the witness has not given any further details.
However, even his said statement that accused Nos.3 and 4 were irritating the deceased also was denied in his cross-examination.
The evidence of P.Ws.3 and 4 is also of no addition to what P.W.1 has stated.
P.W.3, the mother of the deceased has stated that the deceased was telling her that her (deceased's) sister-in-law was troubling her a lot and was not allowing to speak with her husband.
She also stated that, after three months of the marriage of the deceased all the four accused subjected her to trouble.
Except stating that the deceased was subjected to trouble, the witness has nowhere mentioned as to what the alleged trouble was.

Since P.W.1 and P.W.3 being the brother and mother of the deceased respectively and claimed to have heard about the alleged ill-treatment to the deceased by the accused from the mouth of none else than the deceased herself, obviously, it was expected by them to know more details about the alleged ill-treatment, harassment or cruelty.
In such an event, it was expected of both the witnesses to give the instances of the alleged cruelty or harassment said to have been meted to the deceased by the accused.

If, according to both these witnesses, the alleged cruelty by the accused upon the deceased being a regular phenomena till the death of the deceased, then,
several of the instances of alleged cruelty alleged to have been meted to the deceased, could have been narrated by these two important witnesses.
However, the prosecution has not made any effort in eliciting any details from these witnesses except eliciting the words from them as 'irritation' and 'trouble' respectively.
21. Another witness, who speaks about the alleged cruelty upon the deceased by the accused, is P.W.4, the uncle of the deceased.

The said witness, in his examination- in-chief, has stated that when the deceased had visited her parental home lastly, then he came to know that the accused were harassing her asking her to bring more money.
However, the same was denied in his cross- examination from the accused side.

Except stating that he came to know that accused were harassing the deceased asking her to bring more money, even this witness has also not given any further details as to through whom he came to know about the alleged harassment, when the alleged harassment was practiced by the accused,
whether the said harassment was a single instance or was repetitive etc.

Thus, his statement that he came to know that the deceased was subjected to harassment by the accused would not by itself is sufficient to hold that the ingredients of Section 498A of IPC has been fulfilled by the prosecution.

22. In addition to the above witness, the prosecution also examined P.W.6 (C.W.7)-Kotresh, P.W.7 (C.W.12)- Basavanthamma, P.W.8 (C.W.13)-Rajabakshi, stating that they being the tenants under the accused were aware of the cruelty by the accused meted upon the deceased.
However, these witnesses, except stating that they were tenants under the accused, have not supported the case of the prosecution with respect to the alleged cruelty.

Both these witnesses have stated that they do not know anything about the death of the deceased Smt. Jayashri.

P.W.8 has stated that it was only in the morning after the alleged incident, he came to know about the incident of death of Smt. Jayashri, however, he did not come to know the details of cause of her death.
Thus, the evidence of P.W.6, 7 & 8 also would not be of any help to the prosecution to show that the accused had subjected the deceased to cruelty.

Therefore, in the absence of essential evidence to show that there was any conduct of the accused which led the deceased to sustain bodily harm and the said conduct was willful on the part of the accused or that there was any harassment from them towards the deceased for valuables to be brought by her, it is not safe to hold that the prosecution has proved the alleged guilt against the accused punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
23.
The accused No.1 was charged by the Trial Court for the offence punishable under Sections 302 and 304B of IPC read with Section 34 of IPC.

The accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 were charged for the offence punishable under Section 304B of IPC.
24.
It is not in dispute that the death of the deceased Smt. Jayashri on the intervening night of 17th and 18th April 2015 was an unnatural death.

The contention of the prosecution was that it was a murder, whereas the defence of the accused was that the deceased being annoyed with the alleged act of her parents in sending her back to her marital home forcibly, voluntarily stabbed herself with a knife, thus it was a suicide.
25.
The witnesses who speak about the nature of death of the deceased Smt. Jayashri are mainly P.W.1, P.W.2, P.W.3 and P.W.4.
P.W.1, the complainant in his complaint at Ex.P.1 had suspected the death of his sister Smt.Jayashri as murder committed by the accused.
Even in his evidence as P.W.1 also, he has stated that the accused have committed the murder of his sister.

Except stating that by seeing dead body of his sister in the Government Hospital at Kudligi, he noticed stab injury in the abdomen of the deceased and the contusion on the neck, the witness has not stated as to how he arrives at the opinion that the death was a murder.
However, he has further added in his evidence that a knife was found beneath the bed on the cot which knife was washed and kept there.
He has also stated that accused No.1 stated that he had washed the knife and kept it there.
Thus, he has made an attempt to show that there were reasons for him to say that it was a murder.

However,

P.W.2 (C.W.2) - Badrinarayan, a pancha for scene of offence panchanama as per Ex.P.2, pancha for the seizure of clothes of the deceased under Ex.P.13 and also a pancha for inquest panchanama at Ex.P.12, has stated that when he saw the dead body in the hospital at Kudligi, he noticed a stab injury on the abdomen of the deceased and swelling of the neck.
A panchanama was drawn by the Tahasildar in his presence.
However, in his cross-examination, he has stated that about swelling on the neck of the dead body, no mentioning is made in the inquest panchanama.
Except this, nowhere in his evidence, the witness has stated as to the opinion of the panchas about the nature of the death of the deceased Smt. Jayashri.
However, the inquest panchanama at Ex.P.12 shows that the deceased Smt. Jayashri was stabbed by accused No.1 on the night of the incident with a knife and has caused her murder.
However, in the cross-examination of this witness from the accused side, the said opinion of the pancha to the inquest panchanama was seriously denied and disputed.

P.W.3, the mother of the deceased though has stated in her examination-in-chief that the accused,
who are four in number, killed her daughter, but nowhere her evidence shows as to on what basis she has concluded that the death of her daughter was due to killing and that too by the accused.

P.W.4, the uncle of the deceased, though has stated that he noticed three injuries on the abdomen of the deceased and the he came to know that the four accused have caused her murder, but he also nowhere has stated as to on what basis he concluded that it was a murder that too committed by the accused.
The evidence of P.W.1, P.W.3 and P.W.4 that the death of the deceased was a murder, was denied in their cross-examination from the accused side.
As such, merely by the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.4, it cannot be concluded that the death of the deceased Smt. Jayashree was a murder and it was committed by the accused.
In that regard, the medical evidence placed by the prosecution is also required to be analysed.
26. P.W.5 (C.W.14) - Dr. Ravindrakumar, the then Medical Officer at Kudligi, has stated that he conducted autopsy on the dead body of Smt. Jayashri on 18.04.2015.
He stated that he noticed an incised wound on epigastric region measuring 2 x 0.5 inch with depth of 4 inch, penetrating into the abdominal cavity.
He stated that subcutaneous fat was protruding from the wound.

The witness has further stated that, after dissecting the body, he noticed a deep penetrating wound in anterior abdominal wall measuring 2 x 0.5 x 4 inch, tearing of peritoneum layer in the epigastric region.
He also noticed an injury to the larger intestine measuring 1.5 x 0.3 inch, and also the liver had penetrating injury on the left lobe measuring 2 x 0.5 x 2 inch.
He noticed the collection of approximately 2.5 litres of blood in the peritoneal cavity.
With this observation, the doctor has opined that death was due to hemorrhagic and oligaenic shock secondary to deep penetrating stab injury over the upper abdomen.
